exposure: maternal hepatitis B core antibody (HBcAb) status
outcome: HBsAb positivity rate and titer in infants
cohort: The study included 37,557 pregnant women who underwent prenatal screening in Yinchuan, China, from whom 947 HBsAg-positive pregnant women and their 960 neonates, as well as 29 HBsAg-negative pregnant women and their 30 neonates, were selected for analysis.
finding: The study found that delivery by cesarean section, maternal HBeAg positivity, and both low and high maternal viral loads were significantly associated with HBsAg positivity in neonatal cord blood.
mod_finding: Delivery by cesarean section was found to be strongly associated with a lower adjusted odds ratio (0.52) for cord blood HBsAg positivity.
cross-section timing: Data was collected from January 2017 to December 2021.
